observations: Torah 90 contains exactly one bechina edge in the current dataset (ארץ העליונה ↔ שכינה), yielding one package. The gap analysis identifies one additional bechina pair from the source text (חטאים ↔ חסרונות), but this pair constitutes only 2 nodes — the threshold for a standalone new package requires 3 or more concepts forming an independent domain. Furthermore, the חטאים/חסרונות pair is not an independent conceptual domain in this Torah: it describes the raw state that the tikkun (simcha) addresses, and is fully subordinate to the eitza chain rather than constituting its own bechina cluster. There are no 3+ concepts in the source text with explicit bechina language that form a domain not covered by Package 1 (Shekhinah). The teaching's structure does not support additional packages: it is a micro-Torah of a single interpretive move (bechina: ארץ = שכינה) in support of a single eitza argument (simcha → tikkun).
